Check the attached image before choosing each primitive kind. Use `rect` for visibly square corners and `round_rect` only for visibly rounded corners. Draw a line or path only when its stroke is visible in the source image; do not invent guide lines or decorative strokes. Preserve visible internal structures inside containers.

For small native icons, reconstruct the observed silhouette and internal geometry rather than replacing it with a generic symbol. Preserve the reference's visible icon background tile, actual tab/roof shape, front edge, folded corner, border thickness, fill colors, and internal marks where present. A light background square behind an icon is part of the component if visible; do not erase it as incidental whitespace. Use component-local coordinates based on the observed outline, with separate native paths/polygons/lines for the fold and interior marks. Repeated icons should share the same geometric template when their silhouettes match, with only the observed dimensions and positions changed. Keep directory branches separate from labels and icons, and preserve their actual endpoints and junctions. Do not put labels into icon crops, invent outlines around unoutlined folders, simplify away visible folds, or replace editable icon geometry with raster assets. Treat any ellipsis recognized as text as an independent text component.
